questions.question: The West Bengal workplace safety guidelines (2025) specify that night shifts for women must include ________________.

options.text: at least two-third female staff or 20 women, whichever is higher
at least 10 women or one-third of the total staff, whichever is higher
at least 50% female security personnel on every shift

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**at least 10 women or one-third of the total staff, whichever is higher**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of West Bengal** introduced new safety guidelines for women in **2024-2025** to ensure a secure working environment, specifically targeting those working during night hours.
 
• As per the notification, women should be engaged in night shifts only in groups, and the strength of such groups should be **at least 10 women or one-third of the total staff, whichever is higher**. This measure is designed to prevent isolation and enhance collective security.
 
• The guidelines specify that a night shift for this purpose is defined as any work performed between **7:00 PM** and **6:00 AM**.
 
• The **employer** or the head of the establishment is held responsible for ensuring that these numbers are maintained and that security protocols are strictly followed.
 
• The policy also suggests that, wherever possible, women should be avoided for night shifts unless adequate security arrangements are in place and the group size requirement is met.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rattirer Sathi (Helpers of the Night):** This is a flagship initiative launched by the **West Bengal** government that includes a mobile application equipped with a **panic button**. The app is directly linked to local **police stations** and the **Police Control Room (PCR)**.
 
• **Safe Transport:** It is mandatory for employers to provide **security-vetted transport** facilities for women working night shifts, ensuring safe pick-up and drop-off from their residences.
 
• **Security Measures:** The guidelines mandate that all **private security agencies** employed by establishments must be registered, and their guards must undergo **breathalyzer tests** regularly to ensure they are fit for duty.
 
• **Infrastructure Requirements:** Workplaces must have high-quality **CCTV cameras** installed in all sensitive areas, including entrances, exits, and **dark zones**, with a dedicated team monitoring the footage **24/7**.
 
• **Restrooms and Hygiene:** Establishments are required to provide separate, well-lit, and secure **washrooms** and **restrooms** for female employees, which must be located in safe areas of the building.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Identification:** Every employee, including **security personnel** and **contractual staff**, must wear a visible **Identity Card** at all times to prevent the entry of unauthorized persons.
 
• **Dark Zone Mapping:** Authorities must conduct a "safety audit" to identify **dark zones** (poorly lit areas) within the premises and ensure they are immediately illuminated with **LED lights**.
 
• **Duty Rosters:** The **Health Department** and **Home Department** have been tasked with monitoring the implementation of these rosters to ensure that no woman is forced to work alone or in an understaffed environment during the night.
 
• **Emergency Response:** In case of any emergency, the **100/112 helpline numbers** should be prominently displayed across the workplace for immediate assistance.
</ul

questions.question: On 24 July 2025, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways hosted which event in New Delhi to deliberate on financial strategies for India’s maritime future?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maritime Financing Summit, 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Maritime Financing Summit, 2025** was organized by the **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways** (MoPSW) on **24 July 2025** in **New Delhi**.
 
• The summit served as a critical platform to deliberate on **financial strategies** and **investment frameworks** necessary to propel India toward its goal of becoming a global maritime power.
 
• The primary objective of the event was to foster a dialogue between **policymakers**, **financial institutions**, and **industry stakeholders** to unlock the investment potential within the maritime sector.
 
• The discussions were strategically aligned with the **Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047**, which envisions an investment of over **Rs. 80 trillion** to transform the maritime infrastructure of the country.
 
• The event highlighted the importance of **Public-Private Partnerships (PPP)** and innovative funding mechanisms like **Maritime Development Funds** to support port modernization and shipping fleet expansion.
 
• Key focus areas included **sustainable financing** for green shipping initiatives and the enhancement of **Ease of Doing Business** in the maritime financial ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047:**
 
 
• Launched to outline the roadmap for the next **25 years**, this vision aims to increase the capacity of Indian ports to **10,000 MTPA** (Million Tonnes Per Annum) by **2047**.
 
• It focuses on **port-led industrialization**, **coastal shipping**, and the development of **Smart Ports** through **digitization** and **Automation**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW):**
 
 
• This ministry is the apex body responsible for formulating and implementing policies related to **ports**, **shipping**, and **inland water transport** in India.
 
• Under the leadership of **Shri Sarbananda Sonowal** (as of recent administrative records), the ministry has prioritized the **Sagarmala Project** to reduce logistics costs.
 
 
 
• **Investment Opportunities in Maritime Sector:**
 
 
• India offers **100% FDI** (Foreign Direct Investment) under the automatic route for **port construction and maintenance projects**.
 
• The **Blue Economy** policy of India aims to contribute significantly to the **national GDP** by utilizing ocean resources sustainably while ensuring environmental conservation.
 
 
 
• **Green Shipping and Sustainability:**
 
 
• The **Harit Sagar Guidelines 2023** emphasize the reduction of **carbon footprints** at ports and the promotion of **renewable energy** integration.
 
• India is working toward establishing **Green Hydrogen Hubs** at major ports like **Deendayal Port** and **Chidambaranar Port**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Logistics Efficiency:** One of the core themes of the **2025 Summit** was to lower India's **logistics cost** from **13-14%** of GDP to the global average of **8%**.
 
• **Global Rankings:** India aims to enter the top **10** in the **Logistics Performance Index (LPI)** by improving port turnaround times and **multimodal connectivity**.
 
• **Major Ports:** Currently, India has **12 Major Ports** and over **200 non-major ports**, which together handle approximately **95%** of the country's foreign trade by volume.
 
• **Shipbuilding Industry:** The government is promoting the **Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy (SBFAP)** to encourage domestic vessel manufacturing and reduce dependency on foreign ships.
</ul

questions.question: In June 2025, Union Home Minister Amit Shah unveiled the Flood Hazard Zonation Atlas of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Union Home Minister **Amit Shah** unveiled the **Flood Hazard Zonation Atlas** for the state of **Assam** in **June 2025** to enhance the state's preparedness against annual flood disasters.
 
• The atlas has been developed by the **National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC)**, **ISRO**, in collaboration with the **Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA)**.
 
• It utilizes satellite data acquired over the last **25 years** (from **2000 to 2024**) to identify and categorize flood-prone areas into different risk levels.
 
• This scientific tool is designed to assist **policymakers** and **district administrations** in planning **disaster mitigation**, infrastructure development, and early warning systems.
 
• With the launch of this atlas, **Assam** becomes one of the few states in India, following **Odisha**, to possess a comprehensive, data-driven flood hazard map for better **resource allocation** during emergencies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Context of Assam:**
 
 
• The state is situated in the **Brahmaputra** and **Barak** river valleys, making it highly susceptible to **riverine flooding** and **erosion**.
 
• The **Brahmaputra River**, one of the largest in the world, enters **India** through **Arunachal Pradesh** and flows through the heart of **Assam**, carrying massive amounts of silt and water during the **Monsoon season**.
 
 
 
• **Flood Hazard Mapping Technology:**
 
 
• The atlas uses **Geographic Information System (GIS)** and **Remote Sensing** technologies to map "hazard zones" ranging from **Very High** to **Very Low**.
 
• It factors in **historical flood frequency**, **inundation depth**, and the duration of waterlogging across different **districts**.
 
 
 
• **Disaster Management Framework:**
 
 
• The initiative aligns with the **National Disaster Management Act, 2005**, which mandates states to create comprehensive plans for **prevention** and **mitigation** of disasters.
 
• The **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** provides the overarching guidelines for such digital interventions to minimize the loss of **life and property**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Socio-Economic Impact:** Floods in **Assam** affect nearly **30-40 lakh people** annually and cause heavy damage to **agriculture**, specifically the **Kharif crops**, and wildlife in the **Kaziranga National Park**.
 
• **Early Warning Systems:** The data from the atlas will be integrated into the **Flood Early Warning System (FLEWS)** to provide real-time alerts to **villages** and **revenue circles**.
 
• **Infrastructure Resilience:** By identifying hazard zones, the state government can avoid constructing **critical infrastructure** like **hospitals**, **schools**, and **power stations** in "Very High" risk areas.
 
• **Brahmaputra Board:** Established under the **Brahmaputra Board Act, 1980**, this statutory body works under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti** to manage flood control and drainage in the **North Eastern Region**.
</ul

questions.question: In April 2025, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) mandated banks to move to the '.bank.in' domain by _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**31 October 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **April 2025**, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** issued a significant directive aimed at enhancing the **cybersecurity** framework of the Indian financial sector.
 
• The mandate requires all **scheduled commercial banks**, including public and private sector banks, to migrate their official websites and email services to the **.bank.in** domain by **31 October 2025**.
 
• This transition is designed to provide a **verified and secure** digital identity for banks, making it easier for customers to distinguish between legitimate banking websites and fraudulent ones.
 
• The **.bank.in** domain is a specialized, restricted top-level domain that is exclusively available to **RBI-regulated** entities, ensuring a higher level of trust in the digital ecosystem.
 
• By standardizing on this domain, the **RBI** aims to drastically reduce instances of **phishing**, **identity theft**, and **spoofing** attacks that often target unsuspecting bank customers. ***Hence, the correct answer is 31 October 2025.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The .bank.in Domain:**
 
 
• Unlike generic extensions like **.com** or **.in**, the **.bank.in** domain involves a rigorous verification process conducted by the **Institute for Development and Research in Banking Technology (IDRBT)**.
 
• The **IDRBT**, which is the technical arm of the **Reserve Bank of India**, manages the registration to ensure that only authorized financial institutions gain access.
 
 
 
• **Security Protocols:**
 
 
• Migration to this domain necessitates the implementation of **Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC)**.
 
• **DNSSEC** adds a layer of security by digitally signing **DNS** data, which prevents "man-in-the-middle" attacks and ensures that users are not redirected to malicious servers.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**
 
 
• The **RBI**, established on **1 April 1935**, functions as the central bank of **India** and regulates the banking system under the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**.
 
• It continuously updates its **Cybersecurity Resilience Framework** to combat the evolving nature of digital threats in the global financial landscape.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• The move aligns with global best practices, such as the use of the **.bank** domain in the **United States** and other developed economies, which serves as a "gold standard" for security.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Customer Impact:** After the **31 October 2025** deadline, any banking communication received from a non-**.bank.in** domain should be flagged as potentially fraudulent by customers.
 
• **Compliance:** Banks are required to submit progress reports to the **RBI** regarding their migration status to ensure the deadline is met without disrupting banking operations.
 
• **Scope:** The mandate covers all customer-facing portals, internal communication systems, and official email IDs of bank employees to ensure **end-to-end security**.
 
• **Verification:** The registration process for **.bank.in** includes **multi-factor authentication** for any changes to the domain records, providing an additional safeguard against unauthorized modifications.
</ul

questions.question: The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) introduced a new Blue Category for industries through a circular in February 2025. Which industries fall under it?

options.text: Essential environmental services like waste-to-energy plants
IT and software service providers such as Infosys

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Essential environmental services like waste-to-energy plants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **February 2025**, the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** issued a circular introducing the **Blue Category** of industries to classify entities providing **essential environmental services**.
 
• This new category includes facilities such as **Waste-to-Energy plants**, **Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs)**, **Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs)**, and **Common Bio-Medical Waste Treatment Facilities**. ***Hence, the statement regarding essential environmental services is correct.***
 
• The primary objective behind this reclassification is to recognize the **positive environmental footprint** of these services, which were previously categorized under **Red** or **Orange** due to their operational emissions, despite their role in pollution control.
 
• By moving these industries to the **Blue Category**, the government aims to facilitate **Ease of Doing Business** and promote a **Circular Economy** by providing a more supportive regulatory framework for waste management and recycling infrastructure.
 
• The classification helps in distinguishing **pollution-generating industries** from those dedicated to **pollution mitigation and resource recovery**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Industrial Categorization in India**:
 
 
• The **CPCB** introduced a classification system based on the **Pollution Index (PI)**, which is a number from **0 to 100**. A higher PI indicates a higher degree of pollution potential from the industrial sector.
 
• **Red Category**: Includes industries with a **Pollution Index** score of **60 and above**. These are high-polluting industries like **refineries**, **tanneries**, and **thermal power plants**.
 
• **Orange Category**: Includes industries with a **Pollution Index** score between **41 and 59**. These have a moderate pollution footprint, such as **food processing** or **pharmaceutical formulations**.
 
• **Green Category**: Includes industries with a **Pollution Index** score between **21 and 40**. These are low-polluting industries like **small-scale tea processing** or **poultry farms**.
 
• **White Category**: Includes industries with a **Pollution Index** score up to **20**. These are practically non-polluting and do not require **Consent to Operate (CTO)**, such as **solar power generation** or **IT and software services**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Impact**: The introduction of the **Blue Category** allows these essential services to obtain **Consents (CTE and CTO)** under a streamlined process, often with longer validity periods compared to **Red** category industries.
 
• **Date of Implementation**: The directive was officially circulated in **February 2025**, marking a shift in India’s environmental governance from a purely emission-based view to a **utility-based view** of industrial activity.
 
• **Authority**: The **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** is a statutory organization constituted in **September 1974** under the **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974**. It also serves under the **Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981**.
 
• **Sustainable Development**: This move aligns with India's commitments toward **Net Zero** goals and efficient waste management under the **Swachh Bharat Mission**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following famous footballers was awarded the United States Presidential Medal of Freedom in January 2025, the highest civilian honour of the United States of America?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lionel Messi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **January 2025**, the legendary Argentine footballer **Lionel Messi** was honored with the **Presidential Medal of Freedom** by the United States government.
 
• The award was conferred by **President Joe Biden**, recognizing Messi's extraordinary contributions to the world of sports and his massive influence on the cultural fabric of the **United States** since his move to the **Major League Soccer (MLS)**.
 
• Lionel Messi joined the American club **Inter Miami CF** in **July 2023**, a move that is credited with revolutionizing the popularity of football (soccer) in North America.
 
• The **Presidential Medal of Freedom** is the **highest civilian honour** in the **United States**, typically awarded to individuals who have made an "especially meritorious contribution to the security or national interests of the United States, world peace, cultural or other significant public or private endeavors."
 
• Messi’s recognition follows his historic achievement in leading **Argentina** to victory in the **2022 FIFA World Cup** and his record-breaking **8 Ballon d'Or** titles. ***Hence, the correct answer is Lionel Messi.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Presidential Medal of Freedom:**
 
 
• Established by **President John F. Kennedy** via **Executive Order 11085** in **1963**, it succeeded the original Medal of Freedom established by **Harry S. Truman** in **1945**.
 
• While usually awarded to **U.S. citizens**, it can also be granted to foreign nationals who have made significant contributions to the world or the interest of the **USA**.
 
• Other notable sports figures who have received this medal include **Tiger Woods** (2019), **Michael Jordan** (2016), and **Muhammad Ali** (2005).
 
 
 
• **Impact of Lionel Messi in the USA:**
 
 
• Since joining **Inter Miami**, Messi has significantly increased the commercial value of **MLS**, leading to record-breaking **Apple TV** subscriptions and ticket sales.
 
• His presence is seen as a crucial catalyst for the growth of the sport in the **USA** ahead of the **2026 FIFA World Cup**, which the country will co-host.
 
• In **2023**, he was named **TIME Magazine's Athlete of the Year**, further cementing his status as a global icon beyond just the football pitch.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lionel Messi's Achievements:** He holds the record for the **most goals scored in La Liga** (474) and has won **44 professional trophies**, making him the most decorated player in football history.
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Cristiano Ronaldo:** A Portuguese legend currently playing for **Al Nassr** in **Saudi Arabia**; while a global superstar, he has not been awarded the U.S. Presidential Medal of Freedom.
 
• **Neymar Jr.:** A Brazilian forward playing for **Al Hilal**; known for his skill but lacks this specific American civilian honor.
 
• **Luis Suarez:** A teammate of Messi at **Inter Miami** and an **Uruguayan** legend, but he was not the recipient of the award in **2025**.
 
 
 
• The award ceremony in **January 2025** marked one of the final significant acts of the **Biden administration** regarding civilian recognitions for international figures.

__
 
• The **World Health Summit (WHS) Regional Meeting 2025** was hosted in **New Delhi**, **India**. This marked a historic milestone as it was the **first time** that this prestigious regional health forum was held in the **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• The meeting was organized by the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)**, Government of India, in close collaboration with the **World Health Summit** foundation based in **Berlin**.
 
• The summit, held in **April 2025**, brought together global health leaders, researchers, and policymakers to discuss the specific health challenges and opportunities within the **Global South** and the **Asian region**.
 
• The primary focus of the **2025 Regional Meeting** was to foster international cooperation in areas such as **pandemic preparedness**, **digital health innovations**, and strengthening **primary healthcare systems**.
 
• By hosting this event, **India** showcased its leadership in global health, particularly highlighting its role as the **'Pharmacy of the World'** and its efforts towards achieving **Universal Health Coverage (UHC)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Health Summit (WHS):** 
 
 
• The **World Health Summit** was founded in **2009** on the occasion of the 300th anniversary of the **Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin**.
 
• While the main annual summit always takes place in **Berlin**, **Germany**, the **Regional Meetings** are held annually in different parts of the world, hosted by the member of the **M8 Alliance** that holds the regional presidency for that **year**.
 
 
 
• **M8 Alliance:** 
 
 
• The **M8 Alliance of Academic Health Centers, Universities and National Academies** is the academic foundation of the **World Health Summit**.
 
• It is a network of currently **31 members** in **20 countries**, including the **InterAcademy Partnership (IAP)**, which represents the national academies of medicine and science in over **100 countries**.
 
 
 
• **Themes of the Meeting:** 
 
 
• The **2025 New Delhi** meeting emphasized the **'One Health'** approach, which recognizes the interconnection between **people**, **animals**, and our **shared environment**.
 
• Discussions also revolved around the integration of **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** in healthcare and the implementation of the **National Digital Health Mission (NDHM)** model on a global scale.
 
 
 
• **Previous Meetings:** 
 
 
• Before the **2025** meeting in **India**, other regional meetings have been held in locations such as **Melbourne (2024)**, **Rome (2022)**, and **Coimbra (2019)**. Each meeting addresses unique regional priorities aligned with the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 3)**.
 
 
 
• **India's Healthcare Initiatives:** 
 
 
• The selection of **New Delhi** as a venue aligns with India's successful initiatives like **Ayushman Bharat**, which is the **world’s largest** government-funded healthcare program, providing coverage to over **500 million** citizens.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following organisations successfully flight-tested the nuclear-capable Agni-5 missile in August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** successfully conducted a flight test of the **Agni-5** missile in **August 2025**, reinforcing India's strategic deterrent capabilities.
 
• **Agni-5** is an **Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM)** developed indigenously by **DRDO**, capable of striking targets at ranges exceeding **5,000 kilometres**.
 
• The missile is a **three-stage solid-fueled** engine system, designed to carry **nuclear warheads** weighing over **1,000 kg**, significantly enhancing India's second-strike capability.
 
• This specific test in **2025** focused on validating advanced sensors and new guidance systems to ensure high accuracy for long-range strikes. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **Agni-5** incorporates **Canister Launch** technology, which allows for road mobility and reduces the time required for launch, ensuring a higher level of operational flexibility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evolution of the Agni Series:**
 
 
• The **Agni missile** family is a critical component of India's **minimum credible deterrence**. It began under the **Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP)**, managed by **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam** in the early **1980s**.
 
• While **Agni-1** had a range of **700 km**, the series evolved through **Agni-2 (2,000 km)**, **Agni-3 (3,000 km)**, and **Agni-4 (4,000 km)**, culminating in the **Agni-5 ICBM**.
 
• Newer variants like **Agni Prime (Agni-P)** have also been developed as **two-stage**, canisterized missiles with ranges between **1,000 and 2,000 km**.
 
 
 
• **Technical Features of Agni-5:**
 
 
• The missile uses a **Ring Laser Gyroscope (RLG)** based high-accuracy **Inertial Navigation System (INS)** and **Micro Navigation System (MINGS)** to reach its target with precision.
 
• Recent advancements in the Agni-5 program include **Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle (MIRV)** technology, which allows a single missile to deliver multiple warheads to different locations.
 
• The **Agni-5** project was led by mission directors and scientists at the **Advanced Systems Laboratory (ASL)**, a premier lab of **DRDO** located in **Hyderabad**.
 
 
 
• **Organization Roles:**
 
 
• **ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation):** Primarily responsible for India's **space program**, satellite launches, and planetary exploration, established in **1969** with headquarters in **Bengaluru**.
 
• **HAL (Hindustan Aeronautics Limited):** An aerospace and defence company headquartered in **Bengaluru**, primarily involved in the design and manufacture of **fighter jets, helicopters, and gas turbine engines**.
 
• **BDL (Bharat Dynamics Limited):** Acts as the **manufacturing base** for guided weapon systems in India, producing missiles designed by **DRDO**, founded in **1970** in **Hyderabad**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **DRDO Background:** Established in **1958** by merging the **Technical Development Establishment (TDEs)** of the Indian Army and the **Directorate of Technical Development & Production (DTDP)** with the **Defence Science Organisation (DSO)**.
 
• It functions under the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India, and is headed by the **Secretary, Department of Defence R&D**.
 
• The **Agni-5** flight tests are usually conducted from the **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island** (formerly Wheeler Island) located off the coast of **Odisha** in the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• The success of the **Agni-5** puts India in an elite group of nations possessing **ICBM** technology, which includes the **USA, Russia, China, France, and the UK**.
</ul

questions.question: "Operation Abhyaas", a nationwide civil defence mock drill held on 7 May 2025, was organized by which of the following in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Home Affairs**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Abhyaas** is a significant **nationwide civil defence mock drill** organized by the **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** on **7 May 2025**.
 
• The primary objective of this exercise was to assess and enhance the **preparedness, coordination, and response capabilities** of various civil defence units and local administrative bodies across **India**.
 
• The drill simulated multiple emergency scenarios, including **natural disasters** and **man-made crises**, to test the real-time mobilization of **Civil Defence volunteers** and **Home Guards**.
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs** orchestrated the event to ensure that the **Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)** for disaster management are effectively implemented at the **grassroots level**.
 
• This initiative is part of the government's broader strategy to strengthen **internal security** and **community resilience** during large-scale emergencies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA):**
 
 
• The **MHA** is a nodal ministry of the **Government of India** responsible for the maintenance of **internal security** and domestic policy.
 
• It oversees the **Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs)** and provides administrative support to the **Union Territories**.
 
• The ministry is headed by the **Union Home Minister**, who is a senior member of the **Union Council of Ministers**.
 
 
 
• **Civil Defence in India:**
 
 
• **Civil Defence** measures are designed to protect the **civilian population** against any hostile attack or disaster.
 
• In **India**, the **Civil Defence Act, 1968**, provides the legal framework for the organization and operation of civil defence bodies.
 
• The **Directorate General of Fire Service, Civil Defence & Home Guards** under the **MHA** coordinates these activities nationwide.
 
 
 
• **Disaster Management Framework:**
 
 
• The **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, led to the creation of the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)**, which is chaired by the **Prime Minister**.
 
• Mock drills like **Operation Abhyaas** are essential tools used by the **NDMA** and **MHA** to identify gaps in the **disaster response mechanism**.
 
 
 
• **Other Entities:**
 
 
• **NITI Aayog:** A policy think tank of the **Government of India** that focuses on **sustainable development goals** and cooperative federalism, but does not usually organize field-level mock drills.
 
• **Ministry of Finance:** Responsible for the **economy of India**, including taxation, financial legislation, and the **Union Budget**.
 
• **Indian Institute of Administrative Sciences:** Primarily an **academic and training institution** rather than an operational body for nationwide civil defence drills.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographical Reach:** The drill on **7 May 2025** covered all **States** and **Union Territories**, making it one of the largest **civil-military coordination** exercises in recent years.
 
• **Stakeholder Involvement:** Apart from the **MHA**, the exercise saw participation from the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)**, **State Disaster Response Forces (SDRF)**, and various **Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs)**.
 
• **Technological Integration:** During **Operation Abhyaas**, advanced communication tools and **drones** were deployed to monitor response times and simulated **search and rescue** operations.
</ul
